index.note: Flow opens the room: a 1968 chalet taken down to the studs, the cabin and mid-century idea in grey, then two chapters (the exterior, the main level) that are also their sections' titles; the blend's words move into the main level's row, and the closing keeps the 400 square feet.
index.stand: A 1968 Pacific Northwest chalet, taken down to the studs and rebuilt inside and out. | Mixing cabin and mid-century was the whole idea.
abs: The Mountain View chalet hadn't been rethought since the '90s.

The chalet no longer disappears.g: and the chalet no longer disappears against the evergreens on cloudy days
li: The stairs | they run down from the deck to a stone patio off the side of the house.
At night | new fixtures light the stairs, with string lights over the patio.
The front | the way up to the door climbs a rocky slope.

Every seat faces the trees.t: The main wall got sliding glass doors 16 feet across,
Every seat faces the trees.g: so the tree canopy is what you look at from every seat in the room
li: The A-frame | wood plank all the way up, with a triangular window under the peak and a skylight.
Cabin | reclaimed pine floors in mixed plank widths, exposed beams, painted stone and the antlers.
Mid-century | the sputnik chandelier, the Malm fireplace, the walnut dining set and the leather sling chair.

decks.The chalet no longer disappears: A gray-brown with a warm undertone went on the siding, and white on the railings.
decks.Every seat faces the trees: The furniture is kept simple on purpose so it doesn't compete with what's outside the glass.

lines.The 1968 structure was sound: The structure was sound, so the rebuild kept it. | The blue carpet and the dated railings went.
